t: JSON validator and text document formatter
Free tool for strict JSON validation and instant formatting in your browser, with the first error and its location diagnosed while preserving data order.
Validate JSON syntax and format instantly

Yes, you can check text instantly here and turn it into a clear formatted view when it is valid. Paste the document into the box, then validate to see the status, or format to get consistent lines and spacing that preserve the order of members and array elements. Validation follows strict rules, so comments, trailing commas, unquoted keys and unknown values are rejected, and the exact first offending position is reported. If validation succeeds, an easy-to-read copy appears without changing the meaning or data order. If an error appears, the original text stays as is for editing, and no incomplete formatted result is shown. Everything happens in your browser, with no file uploads or external connections.
The original text stays available for correction when an error occurs.
Only spaces and line breaks change.
Comments, trailing commas, and unquoted keys are rejected.
Duplicate keys are preserved in the order they appear.
No partial result is shown when the first error is found.
What does the checker consider valid text?
The checker accepts only strict JSON values: objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, and null, and rejects comments, trailing commas, and unquoted keys.
What appears when there is an error?
The first error is described with line, column and offset, the original text stays in the input box for editing, and no formatted result is shown.
No, member and array element order stays the same, only spaces and line breaks change, and duplicate keys are preserved.
Can a document with an error be formatted?
No, formatting runs only after validation succeeds, so you will not get a partial result from an invalid document.
Is the data sent anywhere else?
No, checking and formatting run entirely in your browser, with no uploads or external connections.
